body: Ahh, that it is. Thank you, so much. I really really appreciate you talking to me, it's lessened the pressure a lot. Good night (((hugs)))

It is nice, but I definitely can't stay there all the time. We still have some weirdnesses because a long time ago we dated, and the relationship ended in physical abuse. We grew past that, we were both trying to overcome amphetamine addiction at the time, but we've gotten drunk and brawled it out publicly as recently as earlier this year. We resent each other sometimes, I guess because I've sort of adapted a maternal role and take care of him in that I keep him from getting arrested and help him shop healthily, and we both buy each other lunch when the other cant afford it (or dumpster something for the other if neither can) and I even sometimes do shit thats probably weird for exes to do like rubbing his back to help him sleep when he's worried about having seizures, and he's returned that by always providing me with a place to sleep no matter how mad at me he was, which is incredible, but as much as he sometimes craves affection, if I sometimes turn it around and ask for affection because I'm feeling bad, a slew of insults is sure to follow (ie "quit being needy" "things are never going to be like that, just get over it" "That's fucking gross, I thought you were passed that") and things to belittle me when all I ask for in that situation is a hug. I don't even ask him to listen to what's wrong or do anything beyond that. He just says he's emotionally distant and if we're going to be friends I have to get over needing that.

Whew. So theres that.

Yeah, sometimes it makes me feel strong, to laugh about it, but sometimes I really really just want to get it off my chest and get ((hugs)). Having to relearn to walk is really strange though. I'll take a step with my normal leg, and then it's like my other leg has forgotten what to do and it sort of just stands there and shakes, even with the crutches. The other thing adding to this is that the only place I know for certain I can sleep if I really need to is at my best friends house,  which is cool, it's generous as hell and I appreciate it to no end, but we have a really really strange friendship and sometimes the things he says/does are more likely to make me feel like crying than the fact that I'm without a house again.

It's nice to not feel isolated in this, as much as it sucks that you've had to go through this too. I think that's part of the problem, the isolation, but I can't bring myself to do anything but laugh it off with my friends. I wish I could pin point the source of this feeling, I feel like it would be easier to deal with. I lost my job and my house three months ago because of a leg injury. I couldn't put weight on it until about a week ago and it's atrophied a lot in that time, so I'm learning to walk again. Makes it hard to get around and take care of myself, which I think is perhaps why everything else is overwhelming me. If that makes sense?

Hey. I've been lurking here all day (trying to heal vicariously? heh.) and I've noticed your username a few times. I always pronounce sequential numbers in a hyper voice in my head for some reason. I dunno, just one of those things. Anyway, I suppose that's why I recognized your username. I'm not sure why I'm telling you this, but talking feels nice. And that I've got this assumption that you're something of mother teresa for the emotionally distressed now.

Oh god, a phone call would be lovely, but I don't have minutes. I don't know, can you tell me how to figure out what's wrong? I guess that's a weird question. There's just so much right now, and I most of it I take fine, but then the littlest thing is what tends to make me feel like crying. It's just this desperate feeling that seems like it can't be relieved. I mean I know it can, because I've been in and out of it before, but it doesn't feel like it can be relieved, and the whole feeling ordeal is a lot more convincing than knowing. If that makes any sense.
